dossier.purpose: One skill (skills/webapp-testing) inside Anthropic's anthropics/skills repository. It is a 96-line SKILL.md, one stdlib-only Python helper (scripts/with_server.py) and three Playwright example scripts. It tells an agent to test local web apps by writing its own Python Playwright scripts (headless Chromium). The agent picks one of three paths: static HTML, an already-running server, or starting servers with the helper around a command. The skill is one of 19 in the repo. The Claude Code marketplace lists it only inside the 12-skill `example-skills` bundle (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:25-42). The repo has no dedicated security-procedure skill, and nothing in it mentions Codex.

claims.claim: Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks.
The repo's skills range 'from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows'.
Each skill is self-contained in its own folder with a SKILL.md file containing the instructions and metadata that Claude uses.
Many skills are open source (Apache 2.0); the docx, pdf, pptx and xlsx skills are 'source-available, not open source'.

Skills are 'provided for demonstration and educational purposes only'; behaviour in Claude may differ; 'Always test skills thoroughly in your own environment before relying on them for critical tasks.'
Claude Code: register the repo with `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, then install `document-skills` or `example-skills` (`/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills`).
After installing the plugin, 'you can use the skill by just mentioning it'.
Claude.ai: the example skills are already available to paid plans. Claude API: pre-built skills can be used and custom skills uploaded.
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter; only `name` and `description` are required.
The Agent Skills standard lives at agentskills.io; ./spec ('The Agent Skills specification') and ./template ('Skill template') are listed as repo contents.

SKILL.md: 'Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.'

SKILL.md: test local web apps by writing native Python Playwright scripts. scripts/with_server.py manages server lifecycle for multiple servers. Run scripts with --help first and use them as black boxes.

SKILL.md decision tree: static HTML means read the file for selectors. A dynamic app with no server running means use with_server.py. A server already running means reconnaissance-then-action after waiting for networkidle. Always launch chromium headless.

install.method: Claude Code: register the marketplace. This is the only documented install route that applies to Linux/macOS, and the README gives no OS-specific steps.

Claude Code: install the plugin bundle that contains webapp-testing. The bundle holds 12 skills (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:30-41); there is no standalone webapp-testing plugin. The README also describes an equivalent interactive 'Browse and install plugins' path (README.md:39-43).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or phone-home code in skills/webapp-testing. Its only network code is a TCP readiness poll to localhost (with_server.py:28). Every URL in the skill is the placeholder http://localhost:5173 (SKILL.md:59; examples/element_discovery.py:10; examples/console_logging.py:5). A grep for requests/urllib/http.client/api-key/environ/getenv found only `socket` (with_server.py:18, 28, 30). The skill needs no account or API key. A repo-wide grep for telemetry/analytics vendor terms matched only licence text, an XSD and API documentation, not skill code. Outside the code: the documented install uses Claude Code's marketplace add with the GitHub-style shorthand `anthropics/skills` (README.md:34-37). Playwright/Chromium installation is not documented anywhere in the repo (no 'playwright install' or 'pip install playwright' matches), so its network use is undocumented here. README.md:3 embeds a remote skills.sh badge image, which affects README rendering only.

entry_points.what: Skill entry document (96 lines). Frontmatter has name, description (line 3) and license (line 4). The body holds the decision tree, the with_server.py usage and the reconnaissance-then-action pattern.
Only executable helper (106 lines, stdlib only). main() is at line 35 and the __main__ guard at line 105. CLI: --server/--port pairs (repeatable), --timeout (default 30), then `-- COMMAND`.
Playwright template: lists buttons, links and inputs on http://localhost:5173 and saves a full-page screenshot to /tmp.
Playwright template: drives a local HTML file via a file:// URL and writes screenshots to /mnt/user-data/outputs/.
Playwright template: captures page console messages through page.on('console') and writes them to /mnt/user-data/outputs/console.log.
Claude Code marketplace manifest `anthropic-agent-skills` with 5 plugins. webapp-testing is listed only in plugin `example-skills` (line 41).

code.architecture: Repo layout: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (5 plugin bundles that point at skills/ paths: document-skills 4 skills, example-skills 12, claude-api 1, academy-guide 1, discernment-nudge 1); skills/<name>/ (19 folders, each with SKILL.md); spec/agent-skills-spec.md (3-line pointer to agentskills.io); template/SKILL.md; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Other skills also hold JavaScript, HTML, Bash and XSD files. skills/webapp-testing/ has 6 files: SKILL.md (decision tree, patterns, best practices); scripts/with_server.py (argparse CLI that starts each --server command with subprocess.Popen(shell=True), polls localhost:<port> with socket.create_connection until it answers (30 s default per server), runs the user command with subprocess.run, then terminate()/kill() on every server in a finally block); examples/ (3 Playwright sync-API scripts, headless Chromium); LICENSE.txt. There is no library or package: the agent is expected to write its own Playwright scripts. Per-task loading is described only in skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:86-91: name+description always in context, SKILL.md body when the skill triggers, bundled resources as needed. The loader itself is not in this repo.

code.dependencies: skills/webapp-testing has no manifest, so 0 declared direct dependencies. Implicit: the `playwright` Python package plus a Chromium browser (SKILL.md:54, 57; examples/*.py:1), with no install instructions or version pins anywhere in the repo. with_server.py is stdlib only (subprocess, socket, time, sys, argparse; lines 17-21). code.security_policy: none. There is no SECURITY.md (not in the root or in .github), no CODEOWNERS and no dependabot/renovate config. The only security-flavoured text is authoring guidance: skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:113 says skills must not contain malware or exploit code. It is not a vulnerability-reporting policy.

claim_checks.evidence: Screenshots (examples/element_discovery.py:37; examples/static_html_automation.py:17, 29), console-log capture (examples/console_logging.py:14-18) and DOM/element discovery (examples/element_discovery.py:14-34) are demonstrated. claim_checks.claim: SKILL.md:11-12 and 41-49 say scripts/with_server.py manages server lifecycle for one or more servers.
claim_checks.evidence: with_server.py takes repeatable --server/--port pairs (lines 37-38) and rejects mismatched counts (53-55). It starts each server with Popen(shell=True) and waits for a localhost TCP connect up to --timeout, default 30 s (23-32, 65-82). It runs the command after `--` and exits with its return code (44-46, 88-89), then terminates or kills the servers in finally (91-102). The documented command lines match the argparse definitions. Caveats from reading the code, not executing it: server stdout/stderr are piped but never read (69-74); readiness ignores whether the process exited (23-32); only the shell PID is terminated, with no process-group handling (94-101).

claim_checks.claim: SKILL.md:14 says to run scripts with --help first and not read the source because 'these scripts can be very large'.
claim_checks.evidence: argparse provides --help (with_server.py:36-40), but the help text is a one-line description and does not include the usage examples in the module docstring (lines 2-15). The skill ships one script of 106 lines, so the 'very large' rationale does not match the shipped file.

risks: Scope: README.md:22-24 says the skills are 'for demonstration and educational purposes only'. webapp-testing is guidance for local Playwright automation. The collection has no dedicated security-procedure skill. The 19 SKILL.md frontmatters cover documents, design, API, MCP, testing and comms. Security text is incidental: skills/mcp-builder/reference/mcp_best_practices.md:152-179 (for MCP servers) and skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:113 (an authoring rule).

No assurance infrastructure: 0 test files, no .github/CI, no release workflow, no SECURITY policy, and no tags in the clone (.git/packed-refs:2). The marketplace manifest has one static version, 1.0.0 (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:9). README.md documents no way to pin a version or commit.

Granularity and agent coverage: webapp-testing is listed in the marketplace only inside the 12-skill `example-skills` bundle (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:25-42), and the README documents only bundle-level install (README.md:39-49). Only Claude surfaces are documented (README.md:31-61). The string 'codex' appears nowhere in the repo, so Codex use depends on the external Agent Skills standard (README.md:1, not opened).

Undeclared dependencies: the skill needs the Playwright Python package and a Chromium browser (SKILL.md:54, 57; examples/*.py:1) but ships no requirements file, install command or version pin. Documented commands use `python` (SKILL.md:25, 41, 46-49) while with_server.py's shebang is python3 (with_server.py:1).

Arbitrary command execution: with_server.py runs each --server string through the shell (shell=True, with_server.py:68-74) and then an arbitrary command (line 88). The SKILL.md frontmatter declares no allowed-tools (SKILL.md:1-5), so execution is governed by the host's permission settings. SKILL.md:14 and 85 tell the agent to treat scripts as black boxes and not read the source unless needed.

Helper robustness (from code reading, not executed): server stdout/stderr are piped but never drained (with_server.py:69-74), so logs are hidden and a chatty server may block once the pipe buffer fills. Readiness is only a localhost TCP connect (line 28) and does not detect an exited process, so a failed start waits the full timeout and a stale listener on the port passes (23-32, 79-80). Cleanup terminates only the shell process (94-101), so children of compound commands such as 'cd backend && python server.py' may be left running.

Examples are not portable as written: examples/console_logging.py:31 and examples/static_html_automation.py:17, 29 write to /mnt/user-data/outputs/, a path nothing in the repo creates or explains. console_logging.py's open() would raise FileNotFoundError where that directory is absent. examples/element_discovery.py:37 and SKILL.md:69 use /tmp. URLs and selectors are placeholders (localhost:5173, 'path/to/your/file.html', 'text=Click Me').

Licensing and provenance at collection level: there is no root LICENSE, and licences are per skill. webapp-testing is Apache-2.0, but docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx are proprietary 'all rights reserved' (skills/docx/LICENSE.txt:1-30). doc-coauthoring, which is in example-skills, has no LICENSE.txt or license frontmatter (skills/doc-coauthoring/SKILL.md:2-3). THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists GPL-3.0 FFmpeg 7.0.2, imageio, Pillow and OFL fonts for other skills (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:7-33, 287-291, 303-359). None of these are in webapp-testing.

checks.statement: SKILL.md:11-12 and 41-49 say scripts/with_server.py manages server lifecycle for one or more servers. Recorded as verified: yes, with these caveats: the documented command lines match argparse; stdout/stderr are piped but never read (69-74); readiness ignores whether the process exited (23-32); only the shell PID is terminated, with no process-group handling (94-101).
checks.note: Every line reference matches. Repeatable --server/--port options with action='append' are at 37-38. The count-mismatch exit is at 53-55. is_server_ready (23-32) only polls socket.create_connection(('localhost', port)) and never checks process.poll(). Popen(shell=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE) is at 69-74, and the pipes are never read. The --timeout default of 30 is at line 39, and the RuntimeError on timeout is at 79-80. The '--' strip is at 44-46, and subprocess.run plus sys.exit(returncode) are at 88-89. The finally block (91-102) calls terminate(), then wait(5), then kill(), with no start_new_session or killpg, so only the shell process is signalled. The SKILL.md:41 and 46-49 command lines parse against argparse lines 37-40. This was static reading only; I did not execute the script.
